summary: This sample is Locky ransomware. It encrypts victim files using the Windows CryptoAPI (CryptEncrypt with RSA/AES), appends the .locky extension, drops a ransom note (\_Locky_recover_instructions.txt), deletes Volume Shadow Copies via vssadmin to prevent recovery, reports encryption statistics to six hardcoded C2 IP addresses over HTTP, and self-deletes after execution. YARA rule Locky_Ransomware_2 matched with 7 distinct string patterns. The binary imports a full cryptographic pipeline (CryptAcquireContextA, CryptCreateHash, CryptHashData, CryptImportKey, CryptSetKeyParam, CryptEncrypt, CryptGenRandom), anti-debugging via IsDebuggerPresent, and HTTP client APIs for C2 communication. Persistence: Not observed in the provided analysis evidence. Exfiltration: Not observed; no tools or mechanisms for data theft were identified in the binary or YARA rule match. Defense impairment: Observed evidence includes the use of vssadmin to delete Volume Shadow Copies, preventing system recovery, and anti-debugging via IsDebuggerPresent to evade analysis, as cited from the binary import analysis.
key_evidence: YARA rule Locky_Ransomware_2 matched with 7 distinct string patterns at offsets 76020-76700
String at 0x4112D4: '.locky' — ransomware file extension appended to encrypted files
String at 0x411310: '\_Locky_recover_instructions.txt' — ransom note dropped on desktop
String at 0x4113EC: '&encrypted=' and 0x4113F8: '&act=stats&path=' — C2 reporting of encryption stats
String at 0x413800: 'vssadmin.exe Delete Shadows /All /Quiet' — deletes shadow copies to prevent file recovery
String at 0x41392C: 'cmd.exe /C del /Q /F "' — self-deletion after payload execution
Imports: CryptAcquireContextA, CryptCreateHash, CryptHashData, CryptImportKey, CryptSetKeyParam, CryptEncrypt, CryptGenRandom from ADVAPI32.DLL — full crypto pipeline for file encryption
Import signals: crypto_encrypt (T1573), http_client (T1071.001), check_debugger (T1622), set_registry_value (T1112), create_process (T1106)
Function FUN_00404044 at 0x404044: complexity=143, 21 string refs, 91 outgoing calls — likely main ransomware orchestration logic

findings.name: Address Space Layout Randomization
findings.consequence: Without ASLR the image loads at a fixed base — a predictable address for ret2libc-style exploitation and ROP gadget pivots.

findings.name: 64-bit high-entropy ASLR
findings.consequence: Without 64-bit entropy the entropy of the address space is reduced relative to the full 64-bit layout.

findings.name: Data Execution Prevention
findings.consequence: Without NX-compat, writable memory can be executable — classic shellcode-on-stack/heap works directly.

findings.name: Control Flow Guard
findings.consequence: Without CFG, indirect calls are unvalidated — vtable and function-pointer overwrites become direct code-flow hijack.

findings.name: Structured Exception Handling
findings.note: no NO_SEH flag — SEH handlers may exist
findings.consequence: The NO_SEH flag claims no SEH handlers exist; if a handler is still present the claim is false — an exception can overwrite the handler chain for control-flow hijack.

findings.name: Signed-image enforcement
findings.consequence: Without forced integrity, a tampered image is not rejected by the loader's integrity checks.

findings.name: Stack cookie (/GS)
findings.consequence: Without a stack cookie, linear buffer overflows can overwrite the return address directly on the stack.

findings.name: Address Space Layout Randomization
findings.consequence: Without ASLR the image loads at a fixed base — a predictable address for ret2libc-style exploitation and ROP gadget pivots.

findings.name: 64-bit high-entropy ASLR
findings.consequence: Without 64-bit entropy the entropy of the address space is reduced relative to the full 64-bit layout.

findings.name: Data Execution Prevention
findings.consequence: Without NX-compat, writable memory can be executable — classic shellcode-on-stack/heap works directly.

findings.name: Control Flow Guard
findings.consequence: Without CFG, indirect calls are unvalidated — vtable and function-pointer overwrites become direct code-flow hijack.

findings.name: Structured Exception Handling
findings.note: no NO_SEH flag — SEH handlers may exist
findings.consequence: The NO_SEH flag claims no SEH handlers exist; if a handler is still present the claim is false — an exception can overwrite the handler chain for control-flow hijack.

findings.name: Signed-image enforcement
findings.consequence: Without forced integrity, a tampered image is not rejected by the loader's integrity checks.

findings.name: Stack cookie (/GS)
findings.consequence: Without a stack cookie, linear buffer overflows can overwrite the return address directly on the stack.
